source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (United States)", "HHS region", "state/territory", "county (if available in state reports)", "metropolitan area (if FluSurv-NET catchment reported)"]

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

Early-season timing (MMWR Week 40, early October 2024) means influenza activity in the United States is typically at baseline or minimal — absence of high case counts is expected and should not be treated as a data gap.
CDC FluView data for Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) may not be publicly released until approximately 2024-10-11 — check for publication lag before flagging as missing.
State health department reporting cadences vary; some states report weekly, others biweekly or monthly — document reporting frequency per source.
Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.
Do not invent or infer URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed source documents during collection.
FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for early season weeks may have suppressed cells (counts <10) — record suppression status rather than imputing zeros.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Influenza from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

CDC FluView data for Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) may not be publicly released until approximately 2024-10-11 — check for publication lag before flagging as missing.
State health department reporting cadences vary; some states report weekly, others biweekly or monthly — document reporting frequency per source.
Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.
Do not invent or infer URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed source documents during collection.
FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for early season weeks may have suppressed cells (counts <10) — record suppression status rather than imputing zeros.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

validation_source_categories: State health department weekly influenza surveillance bulletins
disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (United States)", "HHS region", "state/territory", "county (if available in state reports)", "metropolitan area (if FluSurv-NET catchment reported)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["MMWR week (primary)", "calendar week ending date", "monthly aggregate (secondary)", "daily (if state dashboard provides)"]
count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

top_result_summaries.title: Influenza - Our World in Data
top_result_summaries.snippet: # Influenza. Seasonal flu is a contagious illness caused by the influenza virus. count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

Early-season timing (MMWR Week 40, early October 2024) means influenza activity in the United States is typically at baseline or minimal — absence of high case counts is expected and should not be treated as a data gap.
CDC FluView data for Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) may not be publicly released until approximately 2024-10-11 — check for publication lag before flagging as missing.
State health department reporting cadences vary; some states report weekly, others biweekly or monthly — document reporting frequency per source.
Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.
Do not invent or infer URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed source documents during collection.
FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for early season weeks may have suppressed cells (counts <10) — record suppression status rather than imputing zeros.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC FluSurv-NET influenza hospitalization surveillance week 40 2024 "2024-2025" season rates United States
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: FluSurv-NET is the CDC's population-based surveillance network for laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations, covering select counties in 14 states (~10% of U.S. population). Hospitalization data is a key target field not fully captured by the main FluView weekly report snippet. Targeting week 40 2024 specifically may surface the FluSurv-NET data table or the NCHS mortality surveillance component, filling the hospitalizations and deaths fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC FluSurv-NET weekly hospitalization rate table or NCHS influenza mortality data for week 40 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, FluSurv-NET label, week 40 2024 reference, hospitalization rate per 100,000

validation_source_categories: State health department weekly influenza surveillance bulletins
disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (United States)", "HHS region", "state/territory", "county (if available in state reports)", "metropolitan area (if FluSurv-NET catchment reported)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["MMWR week (primary)", "calendar week ending date", "monthly aggregate (secondary)", "daily (if state dashboard provides)"]
count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

influenza activity level United States [2024-09-29 OR 2024-10-05]
pediatric influenza death United States 2024-2025 season
FluSurv-NET influenza hospitalization rate 2024

Early-season timing (MMWR Week 40, early October 2024) means influenza activity in the United States is typically at baseline or minimal — absence of high case counts is expected and should not be treated as a data gap.
CDC FluView data for Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) may not be publicly released until approximately 2024-10-11 — check for publication lag before flagging as missing.
State health department reporting cadences vary; some states report weekly, others biweekly or monthly — document reporting frequency per source.
Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.
Do not invent or infer URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed source documents during collection.
FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for early season weeks may have suppressed cells (counts <10) — record suppression status rather than imputing zeros.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) covering influenza cases, hospitalizations, deaths, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29 – Oct 5, 2024) marks the official start of the 2024-2025 influenza season and is the primary target for extractable records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (United States)", "HHS region", "state/territory", "county (if available in state reports)", "metropolitan area (if FluSurv-NET catchment reported)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["MMWR week (primary)", "calendar week ending date", "monthly aggregate (secondary)", "daily (if state dashboard provides)"]
count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

Early-season timing (MMWR Week 40, early October 2024) means influenza activity in the United States is typically at baseline or minimal — absence of high case counts is expected and should not be treated as a data gap.
CDC FluView data for Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) may not be publicly released until approximately 2024-10-11 — check for publication lag before flagging as missing.
State health department reporting cadences vary; some states report weekly, others biweekly or monthly — document reporting frequency per source.
Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.
Do not invent or infer URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed source documents during collection.
FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for early season weeks may have suppressed cells (counts <10) — record suppression status rather than imputing zeros.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Influenza from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States, published by the CDC Influenza Division. source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, covering the target week and enabling extraction of hospitalization counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ILINet outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ILINet tracks the percentage of outpatient visits for ILI nationally and by HHS region, providing syndrome-level case data for the target week.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC influenza-associated pediatric mortality surveillance reports for deaths occurring during or reported in the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC tracks influenza-associated pediatric deaths individually; any deaths reported in MMWR Week 40 would be extractable records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published for the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, New York DOH, Florida DOH) publish weekly or biweekly influenza surveillance summaries that may contain subnational case, hospitalization, and death counts for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet reports covering the United States for the week ending 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet and PAHO regional influenza reports aggregate national-level data from member states including the US, providing an independent validation source for case and virus detection counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive dashboard data exports or structured datasets for MMWR Week 40 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The FluView Interactive tool provides downloadable structured data that can serve as an independent validation layer against narrative report extractions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC's case definitions (confirmed, probable, suspected), ILI thresholds, and hospitalization criteria is essential for correct field mapping and count semantics interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC technical reports describing influenza surveillance systems and count semantics for the US 2024-2025 season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature context helps interpret whether reported counts are newly reported, cumulative, or estimated, and clarifies subtype-level reporting conventions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where influenza counts may be conflated with ILI syndrome counts, avian influenza human cases, or COVID-19 co-reporting for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Early-season reports may bundle respiratory illness counts or include novel influenza A detections that require disambiguation before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView weekly reports, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC ILINet, CDC pediatric mortality surveillance, and state/territorial health department influenza surveillance summaries are the primary authoritative sources for extractable influenza case, death, and hospitalization records for the United States during MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05). These sources publish structured weekly data aligned to the target time window.

WHO FluNet, WHO Global Influenza Update, and PAHO regional influenza surveillance reports aggregate US national influenza data and provide independent validation of CDC-reported counts for the target week.

CDC FluView Interactive downloadable datasets, CDC WONDER, and HealthData.gov influenza surveillance open data provide structured, machine-readable records that can validate narrative extraction from weekly reports.

Peer-reviewed studies on US influenza surveillance methodology, 2024-2025 season epidemiology, and case definition standards provide context for interpreting extracted counts and resolving count-semantics ambiguities.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., CIDRAP, Reuters Health, AP) and situation reports may carry early signals of influenza activity or outbreak reports for the United States during the target week, supplementing official surveillance data.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by MMWR week; 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 spans MMWR Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) and the tail of Week 39 (ending 2024-09-28) — prioritize Week 40 data.
CDC ILINet reports percent ILI visits, not raw case counts — extract as surveillance indicator, not confirmed case count.
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population, not absolute counts — note denominator when extracting.
Laboratory-confirmed case counts from state health departments may differ from CDC aggregate totals — record source-specific counts separately.
Pediatric influenza-associated deaths are individually reported to CDC; cumulative season totals may be available even early in the season.
Influenza A subtype proportions (H1N1 vs H3N2) should be captured if reported alongside case counts.
Cases labeled 'influenza-positive' in clinical lab reports may include both A and B — record subtype if available, otherwise use cases_unspecified.
Early-season (September–October) data may reflect low baseline activity; 'no widespread activity' is a valid reportable finding.
State-level data may be reported as activity level categories (minimal, low, moderate, high, very high) rather than numeric counts — capture both if present.
disambiguation_risks: 'Influenza' may co-occur with 'avian influenza' or 'H5N1' in the same report — restrict to human seasonal influenza unless novel strain is explicitly confirmed in humans.
ILI (influenza-like illness) is a syndromic category, not a confirmed influenza diagnosis — do not conflate ILI visit counts with confirmed case counts.
COVID-19 and RSV are frequently co-reported in respiratory surveillance dashboards — ensure extracted counts are influenza-specific.
'Flu' in colloquial usage may refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — context must confirm respiratory influenza.
MMWR week boundaries: Week 39 ends 2024-09-28; Week 40 ends 2024-10-05 — verify week alignment when extracting dated records.
FluSurv-NET catchment areas are not nationally representative — do not extrapolate rates to national totals without adjustment.
Some state reports aggregate influenza A + B together; others separate by type/subtype — record aggregation level explicitly.

Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.
